sources.citation: Zobel, Erik. 2018. The South Babar languages of southwest Maluku. Web page,https://ezlinguistics.blogspot.com/p/south-babar.html
sources.note: Uses Emplawas as the worked example for phonemicising Taber's data (noun suffix -ɛˀ/-e, s < *ll); only stress remark is reconstructive: 'In stressed (= penultimate) position, all four vowels remain distinct' (Proto Southwest Maluku). Nothing synchronic on Emplawas stress.

sources.citation: Steinhauer, Hein. 2009. The sounds of Southeast Babar. In Adelaar & Pawley (eds.), Austronesian historical linguistics and culture history: a festschrift for Robert Blust (Pacific Linguistics 601), 91-105. Canberra.
sources.note: SISTER language (Southeast Babar, sout2883) only: p.96 'Stress does not seem to be phonemic at the word level. Often the same word occurs with different stress in comparable environments.' Emplawas appears only in the language-map discussion (p.94: informants unsure of its status vis-a-vis Tela-Masbuar).

sources.citation: Taber, Mark. 1993. Toward a better understanding of the indigenous languages of Southwestern Maluku. Oceanic Linguistics 32(2): 389-441 (DOI 10.2307/3623199) — the 193-item Emplawas list as re-keyed with Taber's IPA stress marks in Kaiping, Edwards & Klamer (eds.) 2019, LexiRumah 3.0.0, lect empl1237 (188 forms, source taber93)
sources.note: Primary data only (the article text itself is JSTOR-paywalled, Unpaywall is_oa=false). Every polysyllable carries Taber's stress mark; my script tabulation: 104 penult (ˈwosɛʔ 'moon', ˈkule 'star', ˈmukle 'eye', ˈlipe 'hand', ˈpaːki 'woman', ˈlɛtir 'bathe', ˈwuru 'two'), 41 antepenult — nearly all nouns in -ijɛʔ (ˈokijɛʔ 'head', ˈtutijɛʔ 'breast' = root + glide + noun suffix -ɛʔ, which Grimes & Edwards 2026 write oky-o, tuty-o) or with post-tonic schwa (ˈwakəle 'machete', ˈwokəli 'thick'), 8 final (the prefixed numerals woˈlim 'five', woˈlɛm 'six', woˈik 'seven', woˈauw 'eight', reˈɛr 'nine';…

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: Unravelling their prehistory and classification. Berlin: Language Science Press. sec. 4.6.5 Babar, pp. 223-239 (Emplawas data from Edwards 2023a)
sources.note: Historical phonology only. Emplawas is the Babar language 'for which the most phonetic data is available' (p.228); fn.30 gives /e/-/ɛ/ minimal pairs (/we/ 'water' vs /wɛ/ 'rope'); Table 4.61 possessive paradigms (p.239). No statement on Emplawas stress; only the region-wide remark (sec. 3/13) 'While penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages, words with penultimate schwa can have stress on other syllables.'

sources.citation: Edwards, Owen. 2023-2026. Emplawas and languages of the Babar islands: 'Concordance of Southwest Maluku recordings' (SO_f039b46d-9588-485d-9bf8-70b744e1aae7, access U), 'Vowel contrasts 01-05' notes/TextGrids (EMW164.), 'Wordlist 1500-item checking 01-06' notes (EMW311.), and any full Emplawas 1500-item phonetic wordlist in the deposit.
sources.note: Edwards' phonetic field transcriptions and elicitation notes for Emplawas may mark stress systematically; the full 1500-item Emplawas list was not located by title, and the concordance/dictionary material is user-access.
